messages.author: 9b7fbd2e7eee4442
messages.subject: bug in bar chart?
parts:
Hey everyone,
I am having an issue with what seems like a simple plot attached. If you look at it you'll notice that the x axis looks like it was also coordinate transformed along with the y axis, even though I explicitly tell coord_trans to leave x="identity" (I first tried leaving the x out entirely and the result appears to be the same). I just want the y axis to be sqrt coordinate transformed and the x axis to be left alone.

Thanks for your time!

Code to make plot:
library(ggplot2)
dat.6x <- read.table("venter1_6x.sumStats")
df.6x <- data.frame(dat.6x)
names(df.6x) <- c("Method", "Type", "Mapping", "Fraction")
sub.df.6x <- subset(df.6x, Type != "AP")
ggplot(sub.df.6x, aes(Mapping,weight=Fraction,color=Method,fill=Method))+geom_bar(binwidth=1,alpha=0.5,position="identity")+coord_trans(x="identity",y="sqrt")+facet_grid(.~Type)

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: bug in bar chart?
parts:
John, 

Looks like it's because one of your axes is discrete.  I've been playing with it for the last five minutes and looking at the examples and that's the only conclusion I can see. All of the examples have continuous scales on both axes and any translation I attempt also mucks with the x-axis scale. Could be a bug or an oversight in the code or we're missing some very specific method of doing it with only one continuous axis. 

B
